subtopicTitle: Rendering Strategies: CSR vs SSR vs SSG vs ISR vs Server Components (RSC)
problemStatement:
Architectural comparison of Client-Side Rendering, Server-Side Rendering, Static Generation, Incremental Regeneration, and React Server Components.

**Architectural Importance**:
Choosing the wrong rendering pattern causes terrible SEO, slow Time to Interactive (TTI), server over-utilization, and stale data.
interviewTrap: Using SSR for static marketing pages (wasting server CPU on every request) or using pure CSR for public e-commerce stores (hurting SEO and Web Vitals).

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: CSR: Client downloads empty HTML + big JS bundle. SSR: Server renders HTML on every request. SSG: HTML generated once at build time. ISR: SSG with background cache revalidation. RSC: Components execute on the server and stream serialized UI primitives without adding to client JS bundle.

detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals:
## 🏗️ Modern Web Rendering Architecture

### Architectural Trade-offs
| Pattern | TTFB (Initial) | FCP (First Contentful Paint) | TTI (Time to Interactive) | Server Cost | SEO |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **CSR (SPA)** | ⭐ Fast | ❌ Slow | ❌ Slow | ⭐ Zero server CPU | ⚠️ Difficult |
| **SSR** | ⚠️ Moderate | ⭐ Fast | ⚠️ Hydration lag | ❌ High server CPU | ⭐ Excellent |
| **SSG** | ⭐ Blazing | ⭐ Blazing | ⭐ Fast | ⭐ Lowest (CDN) | ⭐ Excellent |
| **ISR** | ⭐ Blazing | ⭐ Blazing | ⭐ Fast | ⭐ Low | ⭐ Excellent |
| **RSC** | ⭐ Fast | ⭐ Fast | ⭐ Zero hydration for server nodes | ⚠️ Moderate | ⭐ Excellent |

### React Server Components (RSC) Paradigm
In traditional SSR, all components must still be bundled and sent to the browser for **hydration**.
In **RSC**:
- Server components **never download to the client**. Their libraries (e.g. Markdown parsers, database clients) add **0 bytes** to the browser JavaScript bundle!
- They stream a compact serialized UI representation directly into the client tree.
